title: Splitting and uniqueness for a derived triangle with separated degrees
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $D(R)$ be the derived category of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K,L\in D(R)$, and suppose that $L$ is isomorphic in $D(R)$ to a bounded complex of projective $R$-modules whose terms vanish outside degrees $[a,b]$. If $H^i(K)=0$ for all $i\geq a$, then $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(L,K)=0$. If $H^i(K)=0$ for all $i\geq a+1$, then every distinguished triangle $K\to M\to L\to K[1]$ splits as an isomorphism $M\cong K\oplus L$ compatible with the triangle; when $H^i(K)=0$ for all $i\geq a$, this splitting is unique.
